title: Limits of Computation
description: How fast can any computer be? Quantum mechanics answers: a system of energy E can pass through at most 2E/(πħ) distinct states a second. A kilogram, converted wholly into computation, runs 5×10⁵⁰ operations a second. Its memory is the entropy of its stuff, capped by the Bekenstein bound; erasing a bit costs kT ln 2 of heat it must shed; and squeeze it too small and it becomes a black hole. Seth Lloyd worked out the ultimate laptop in 2000. Unlocks the Lloyd Engine.

puzzle.goal: Margolus and Levitin: a system of mean energy E above its ground state takes at least πħ/(2E) to reach an orthogonal state. Write the most operations a second, N.
puzzle.name: Margolus Levitin bound
puzzle.ask: Find N for E = @{E} J, with ħ = 1.0546×10⁻³⁴ J s.
puzzle.method: One operation is one step to an orthogonal state; take the reciprocal of the quickest such step.
